transcript: Santa is dead, The North Pole has descended into chaos and we’re at a song and dance bar pageant to honor his memory, put on by a rag tag group of elves and one reindeer. This week only, the downstairs bar at Soho Playhouse has been transformed  for this holiday show, Edelweiss from the same artists behind last year's equally strange and delightful play, The Beastiary, On the Rocks Theatre Company. Like the Beastiary, this show is unabashedly dark and silly at the same time, and it incorporates a strong visual aesthetic that plays into the pageantry style of storytelling. The concept I described at the beginning is super clever, both in terms of the premise and the format of the show. And the original songs by Andrew R Butler here, who you might recognize from the cast of Stereophonic, are super charming but also hit a few more emotional, somber notes as well. The physical production feels pretty fully realized for the format of the show, but the early performance I attended was definitely still finding its rhythm, with some room to improve in the overall flow, especially transitioning from one segment to the next. But the 45 minute performance still breezed by with a sharp sense of humor and just a really clear artistic vision from collaborators who have such a specific shared style. So if you miss this current run, which ends on December 21st, still keep your eye out in case the show returns and Christmases to come. But even if not, still check out on the Rocks Theatre Company because I think they're doing some really special work.
